newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks rally at close on Fed news.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks rally at close on Fed news.

text.p: Argentine stocks staged a relief rally at the close Tuesday after the U.S. Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged, dealers said.

"The market reacted very well once the uncertainty over rates passed," said Dario Lizzano, head of research at Banco Santander. "That was the chief concern of investors, who are now likely to focus again on good local economic fundamentals."
After Monday's flat finish, the blue-chip MerVal index jumped 2.1 percent to 612.68, recouping nearly half of last week's losses.
Lizzano said fresh domestic industrial production data expected Wednesday could help rekindle enthusiasm on the bolsa, which was hurt last week by the jitters on Wall Street.
"Already we've seen a rebound driven by the steel and cement stocks, which may reflect the expected strong recovery in the durable goods sector early next year," said Lizzano.

Traders said they would still keep an eye on developments in New York, especially the U.S. long bond yield which continued its steady advance Tuesday to 6.66 percent from 6.63 percent at the close Monday.

"If Treasuries pierce resistance and the long bond yield tops 6.75 we could see a turning point in the U.S. markets," said one technical analyst. "Despite the Fed's decision on rates, the outlook in New York remains fairly unpredictable."

In the local session floor volume was puny but climbed to 14.5 million pesos from 13.2 million Monday, while over-the-counter turnover surged to 146.5 million pesos from 49.2 million Monday on position-squaring ahead of Friday's options expirations (the bolsa has 72-hour settlements).
The broad market index gained 1.7 percent, with gainers bashing losers 42 to 10 and 16 stocks closing unchanged.

Best main-tier performers were food giant Molinos, which shot up 6.0 percent after announcing the end of its venture with Kraft Foods, steelmakers Siderca and Acindar, up 4.4 percent and 3.2 percent respectively, Telefonica, up 3.8 percent, and pulp and paper maker Celulosa, up 3.3 percent.
The only MerVal loser was power utility Central Costanera, off 2.6 percent.
